_readme: Maps a CoinGecko platform slug to a CAIP-2 chain ID and the CAIP-19 asset namespace used for tokens on it. This file is the ONLY platform truth the build reads; nothing is derived at build time. Confidence: high = exercised in production ingest or ratified by a CASA spec; medium = hand-reviewed against a named source; low = auto name-match or a provisional namespace with no ratified spec. Raising a confidence level or clearing an entry from `unmapped` is the most useful contribution to this repo.

tron.note: CAIP-2 is ratified; there is NO ratified CAIP-19 asset namespace for Tron. "trc20" is this registry's provisional choice.

stellar.note: CoinGecko encodes classic assets as CODE-ISSUER; Soroban SEP-41 contracts need the sep41 namespace instead.

hedera-hashgraph.note: CoinGecko stores the EVM-alias 0x form; the CAIP-19 reference is the shard.realm.num tokenID. Conversion is unresolved — see data/unmapped.

aptos.note: No ratified CAIP-19 for Aptos. "coin" is provisional and does not distinguish coin from fungible-asset (FA) standards.

sui.note: No ratified CAIP-19 for Sui. "coin" is provisional.

elrond.note: MultiversX (CoinGecko still uses the legacy "elrond" slug). No ratified CAIP-19; "esdt" is provisional.

tezos.note: No ratified CAIP-19. FA1.2 vs FA2 is not distinguishable from the CoinGecko identity alone.

algorand.note: No ratified CAIP-19. "asa" (Algorand Standard Asset) is provisional.

hyperliquid.reason: CoinGecko files HyperCore SPOT tokens here (0x + 32 hex), which are indices in Hyperliquid's own order-book state machine, NOT HyperEVM contract addresses. Mapping this slug to eip155:999/erc20 was wrong: it produced 45 rejected rows and would have produced 45 wrong CAIP-19s if the address check had been looser. HyperEVM ERC-20s are mapped separately under the `hyperevm` slug. Needs a CAIP-2 for HyperCore, which does not exist yet.
